P1.evidence: Application read back explicitly — 'I read through the application, so I have a decent understanding.' The frame was three parts, not four: 'I want to get super, super clear on where you're at, where you're trying to get to, what's missing. And then from there, we can map out something for you specifically and talk about some potential next steps.' Frame agreement was taken — 'That'd all sound good?' — and the open question ran verbatim: 'What do you feel we can potentially help you with?'

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight all asked directly. 'Injuries or any health conditions, anything that's limiting' produced the full ankle history. Diet asked and probed for the indulgences. Training week asked and answered in detail. Desk-bound status was assumed rather than asked, and the rep said so out loud: 'I know you're sitting all day. You're at a bank. I would imagine, we didn't talk about that.' Sleep and energy were never asked, which matters here because the prospect twice mentioned back pain tied to how he sleeps.

P3.evidence: 'If you could change like one thing about your body, what would that be?' produced the one-arm pull-up goal. The why-bridge ran well: 'why do you feel like you do have those high standards? Like, why is it so important for you to actually do all this stuff?' Reflected back accurately: 'the primary motive behind this is like, hey, we're planning on having kids, I want to be able to keep up with them kind of long term.' Never asked who else it impacts — the wife and future children were volunteered — and never drove the legacy or identity line beyond the recap.

P4.evidence: The past-attempts history emerged from the prospect's opening monologue rather than from questions. The rep did probe the turning point twice — 'what shifted for you recently, where this has become actually more of a priority?' and 'Was there a specific moment that clicked for you?' — and asked 'what are we feeling that we're missing right now?', which let the prospect name the gap himself as guidance and a roadmap. The 'why can't you stick to it on your own' challenge was never put; the prospect pre-empted it, so the rep never had to earn it.

P5.evidence: The two-year question was run properly and twice, because the prospect did not understand it the first time: 'if we don't address the fitness thing right now and we just continue doing what we've been doing, what does the next two, three, four years look like for you?' It produced real material — depression, going backwards, processed-food bingeing. Then the rep dropped it. No 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', and the line in the sand was asserted by the rep rather than asked of the prospect: 'it sounds like it's kind of time to draw a line in the sand.'

P6.evidence: The commitment check ran but was telegraphed and leading: 'Trevor makes me ask everybody this... I think I already know the answer for this. But if this does make sense, and we do move forward with this, this is something where, hey, dude, you're willing to commit... Is that right?' The prospect answered 'Yeah' and nothing more. The belief question ('do you believe you can actually get there') was replaced by a product question — 'do you feel like this checks off all the boxes as far as having that plan?' A one-word yes obtained from a pre-answered question is exactly the weak yes the phase exists to prevent.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected, so step 1 is a miss and steps 2-4 were never reachable. The call closed with an open invitation — 'feel free to shoot me a message anytime and whenever you're ready to rock and roll' — with no date, no deposit, no hold on the price, and no onboarding booked.

objection_plays.detail: The best-run OC in this batch. Isolation was near-verbatim: 'right now we're not in a like should I do this place where we're going back and forth on if it's the right thing. It's more of a like a how I do this place' and then 'nothing else that's keeping you from being less than 100% certain that this is the right thing and now it's the right time. It's literally just figuring out the finances.' The break-it-up move ran verbatim too: 'most of Trevor's clients do pay for it upfront. But for certain clients... in some cases we actually break it up.' Then it stalled. Of the six financial-picture questions only one ran — 'how much do you typically have liquid at the end of the month?' No credit cards, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no crypto or investments. Instead the rep asked for a credit score, which is not a scripted move, and texted a third-party financing link. The prospect had by then said three times that structure was not the issue, so the whole second half of the play was aimed at the wrong target.

This is what the call died on and not one move was run. The trigger was explicit and repeated: 'just the timing for me is probably not right', 'The timing right now is not great', 'I would happily do it a few months down the road.' None of 'things never slow down', 'when does it actually become the right time', 'the longer you wait the harder this gets — metabolism slows, injuries compound' (which was tailor-made here, given a post-surgical ankle and a stated fear of letting it go too far), 'what if all you had to do was show up', or 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep instead validated the delay — 'It seems like if you do this, you have to literally see your wife less right now' — and the prospect immediately agreed: 'Exactly. So the choice is pretty clear here.' The rep framed the decision as programme versus marriage and then accepted the answer.

Script gap — the prospect who agrees on value, agrees on price, has the capacity, and simply chooses a later start. The playbook has no path for a dated deferral. There was no offer to hold the price, take a deposit against a future start, book a start date for when his wife relocates, or size the deal against the employer reimbursement of $800-1,000 per six months that he raised unprompted. Three concrete commercial levers existed and none is in the script.

notes: Discovery, framing and the money isolation were all run close to the book, and then the rep let a textbook 'not the right time' walk out unchallenged — he not only skipped OD, he supplied the prospect's justification for him. Second coaching point: the commitment check was pre-answered ('I think I already know the answer for this'), which converts the phase into a formality and produced a one-word yes that carried no weight when the price landed.
